80.text: Which of the following is best method of germplasm conservation ?
80.sol: Endangered plants may be preserved in part through seed bank or germplasm bank. The term seed bank sometimes refers to a cryogenic laboratory facility in which the seeds of certain species can be preserved for up to a century or more without losing their fertility. It can also be used to refer to a special type of arboretum where seeds are harvested and the crop is rotated. 5789.subject: Chemistry
5789.text: The most effective coagulating agent for antimony sulphide sol is
5789.sol: According to Hardy-Scheulze rule, the coagulating power of an electrolyte will be higher for ionic components having greater charges or valencies. For coagulating a sol of a particular charge, we add particles of opposite charge. Thus, to coagulate antimony sulphide sol which is negatively charged, we must add an electrolyte with a cation of higher valency. Thus, Al ₂ ( SO ₄ )₃ that has Al ³⁺ , will be most effective for coagulating antimony sulphide.

67552.text: A body of mass 100 gram is tied to a spring of spring constant 8 ~N / m , while the other end of a spring is fixed. 69929.subject: Physics
69929.text: The change in internal energy of the mass of gas, when the volume changes from V to 2V at constant pressure P is ( is the ratio of specific heat at constant pressure to that of volume) ( = C_p C_v )
69929.sol: The change in internal energy of an ideal gas is given by U = nC_v T . The molar heat capacity at constant volume is C_v = R - 1 . Substituting this into the equation for internal energy gives U = nR T - 1 . From the ideal gas equation PV = nRT , at constant pressure P , we have P V = nR T . The change in volume is V = 2V - V = V . Therefore, nR T = PV . Substituting this back into the expression for U , we get U = PV - 1 .

70482.subject: Physics
70482.text: A tuning fork gives 5 beats per second with 40 cm length of sonometer wire. If the length of the wire is shortened by 1 cm , the number of beats is still the same. The frequency of the fork is
70482.sol: Let f_t be the tuning fork frequency. For a sonometer wire, frequency is inversely proportional to length ( f 1/L ), yielding fL = constant . With L₁ = 40 cm and L₂ = 39 cm , we have f₁ 40 = f₂ 39 , so f₂ = 40 39 f₁ . Beat frequencies are |f_t - f₁| = 5 and |f_t - f₂| = 5 . Since f₂ > f₁ , the tuning fork frequency must lie between them to maintain equal beat differences, giving f_t = f₁ + 5 and f_t = f₂ - 5 . Equating these expressions: f₁ + 5 = f₂ - 5 , so f₂ = f₁ + 10 . Substituting 40 39 f₁ = f₁ + 10 gives 1 39

79933.sol: Gross primary productivity is the amount of organic matter produced at given length of time during photosynthesis.

80158.sol: During TCA cycle, first decarboxylation occurs when Oxalosuccinic acid is converted into -ketoglutaric acid and second decarboxylation occurs when -ketoglutaric acid is converted into succinyl CoA.

80179.subject: Botany
80179.text: With reference to factors affecting the rate of photosynthesis, which of the following statements is not correct?
options: Light saturation for C O 2 fixation occurs at 10% of full sunlight

C 3 plants respond to higher temperatures with enhanced photosynthesis, while C 4 plants have a much lower tem
Tomato is a greenhouse crop that can be grown in C O 2 - enriched atmosphere for a higher yield
80179.sol: In C 3 plants, photosynthesis is decreased at higher temperatures due to increased photorespiration. C 4 Plants have a higher temperature optimum because of the presence of pyruvate phosphate dikinase enzyme, which is sensitive to low temperature.

80229.subject: Botany
80229.text: Which of the following plant growth regulators promotes internode elongation prior to flowering in cabbage ?
80229.sol: Gibberellins promote internode elongation just prior to flowering in rosette plants like cabbage, beet, and many other plants with a rosette habit. This phenomenon is known as bolting. Ethephon is a source of ethylene, which promotes fruit ripening and abscission. Abscisic acid acts as a general plant growth inhibitor and stress hormone. Indole butyric acid is a synthetic auxin widely used to induce rooting in stem cuttings. Answer: Gibberellin

80233.subject: Botany
80233.text: The phenomenon which is influenced by auxin and also played a major role in its discovery :
80233.sol: Auxin influences phototropism, i.e., the growth of the plant in response to light stimulus and this phenomenon played a major role in its discovery. Charles Darwin and his son Francis Darwin observed that the coleoptile of canary grass responded to the unilateral illumination by growing towards the light source (phototropism). They concluded that the tip of coleoptile was the source of auxin and was the site of transmittable influence that caused the bending of the entire coleoptile.

It gives equal importance to all characters.
121688.sol: At present phylogenetic classification systems based on evolutionary relationships between the various organisms are acceptable. This assumes that organisms belonging to the same taxa have a common ancestor. We now use information from many other sources too to help resolve difficulties in classification. These become more important when there is no supporting fossil evidence. Numerical Taxonomy which is now easily carried out using computers is based on all observable characteristics. Numbers and codes are assigne

122014.subject: Botany
122014.text: In Cycas, small specialized roots are associated with nitrogen-fixing microorganisms. Identify the name of these roots and their specific symbiotic partner.
122014.sol: In gymnosperms, the roots are generally tap roots. In Cycas, small specialised roots called coralloid roots are associated with nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria. In Pinus, the roots have a fungal association in the form of mycorrhiza. Root nodules with Rhizobium are found in leguminous angiosperms, and pneumatophores are respiratory roots found in mangrove plants like Rhizophora. Answer: Coralloid roots and cyanobacteria

122026.subject: Botany
122026.text: Identify the pteridophyte which belongs to the class Lycopsida and produces two different kinds of spores (macro and micro spores).
122026.sol: According to NCERT, pteridophytes are classified into four classes: Psilopsida, Lycopsida, Sphenopsida, and Pteropsida. The class Lycopsida includes Selaginella and Lycopodium. While most pteridophytes produce only one kind of spore (homosporous), genera like Selaginella and Salvinia produce two kinds of spores, macro (large) and micro (small) spores, and are known as heterosporous. Therefore, Selaginella is the correct answer as it belongs to Lycopsida and is heterosporous. Lycopodium belongs to Lycopsida but is h

122171.subject: Botany
122171.text: Tea and coffee are affected by
122171.sol: The green algae Cephaleuros virescens causes red rust of tea. Thus, destroying the tea leaves. Similar disease is caused by the species of Cephaleuros to coffee plant, piper and Citrus species.

122346.subject: Botany
options: Both a and b are correct

122463.subject: Botany
122463.text: Body covering Phylum A. Chitinous exoskeleton 1. Aschelminthes B. Calcareous shell 2. Annelida C. Segmented body 3. Arthropoda D. Smooth, unsegmented body 4. Mollusca
122463.sol: Arthropoda have a chitinous exoskeleton, Mollusca have a calcareous shell, Annelida have a segmented body, and Aschelminthes have a smooth, unsegmented body.

122512.subject: Botany
122512.text: Select the group in which pneumatic bones are present.
122512.sol: In Aves, pneumatic bones are present.

122728.subject: Botany
122728.text: What happens to the internodes when a shoot tip transforms into a flower?
122728.sol: A flower is a modified shoot wherein the shoot apical meristem changes to floral meristem. Internodes do not elongate and the axis gets condensed. The apex produces different kinds of floral appendages laterally at successive nodes instead of leaves. When a shoot tip transforms into a flower, it is always solitary. The arrangement of flowers on the floral axis is termed as inflorescence. Depending on whether the apex gets developed into a flower or continues to grow, two major types of inflorescences are defined –

123371.subject: Botany
123371.text: Features Types A. Guard Cells in Grasses 1. Dumb-bell shaped B. Epidermal Cells 2. Multicellular, may be branched C. Root Hairs 3. Unicellular elongations D. Trichomes 4. Parenchymatous cells
123371.sol: Guard cells in grasses are dumb-bell shaped, epidermal cells are parenchymatous, root hairs are unicellular elongations, and trichomes are multicellular and may be branched.

123615.subject: Botany
123615.text: What is the key event that occurs at the onset of anaphase?
options: Chromosomes are moved to spindle equator
Chromosomes are aligned along metaphase plate
Spindle fibres attach to kinetochores of chromosomes
123615.sol: At the onset of anaphase, each chromosome arranged at the metaphase plate is split simultaneously and the two daughter chromatids, now referred to as daughter chromosomes of the future daughter nuclei, begin their migration towards the two opposite poles. each chromosome moves away from the equatorial plate, the centromere of each chromosome remains directed towards the pole and hence at the leading edge, with the arms of the chromosome trailing behind. Thus, anaphase stage is characterised by the following key eve

124363.subject: Botany
124363.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): An acrocentric chromosome forms one extremely short and one very long arm. Reason (R): The centromere in an acrocentric chromosome is terminal in position. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
124363.sol: Assertion (A) is true because in an acrocentric chromosome, the centromere is situated close to its end, which results in the formation of one extremely short and one very long arm. Reason (R) is false because a chromosome with a terminal centromere is called a telocentric chromosome, not an acrocentric chromosome. The centromere in an acrocentric chromosome is sub-terminal (close to its end). Therefore, (A) is true but (R) is false. Answer: (A) is true but (R) is false

124617.subject: Botany
124617.text: What is the mathematical expression of the graph?
124617.sol: On plotting the length of the organ against time, a linear curve is obtained. Mathematically, it is expressed as Lt = L0 + rt

124702.subject: Botany
124702.text: Growth Patterns/Models Description A. Arithmetic growth 1. Linear growth curve, constant growth rate. B. Geometric growth 2. Rapid exponential growth phase in the sigmoid curve. C. Lag phase 3. Initial slow growth phase of the sigmoid curve. D. Log phase 4. Sigmoid growth curve, characterized by lag, log, and stationary phases. E. Stationary phase 5. Growth slows down due to nutrient limitation or other factors.
124702.sol: A - 1: Arithmetic growth is characterized by a linear curve due to a constant growth rate. B - 4: Geometric growth is represented by a sigmoid curve with three distinct phases. C - 3: The lag phase is the initial slow phase of the sigmoid growth curve. D - 2: The log phase is the rapid exponential growth phase in the sigmoid curve. E - 5: The stationary phase occurs when growth slows down due to limitations like nutrient depletion.

124933.subject: Botany
124933.text: What is the process of breaking down glucose in several steps to release energy called?
124933.sol: The strategy that the plant cell uses is to catabolize the glucose molecule in such a way that not all the liberated energy goes out as heat. The key is to oxidase glucose not in one step but in several small steps enabling some steps to be just large enough such that the energy released can be coupled to ATP synthesis. How this is done is, essentially, the story of respiration

125270.subject: Botany
125270.text: The first stable product of fixation of atmospheric nitrogen in leguminous plant is
125270.sol: The fixation of atmospheric nitrogen to ammonia is given as N ₂+8 e ⁻+8 H ⁺+16 ATP [ Nitrogenase ] MO - Fe 2 NH ₃+ H ₂+16 ADP +16 Pi The process in which atmospheric nitrogen gets concerted into inorganic nitrogenon (nitrate, ammonia) compounds through microorganisms is called biological nitrogen fixing.

125384.subject: Botany
125384.text: In cyclic photophosphorylation, where does the excited electron cycle back to?
125384.sol: When only PS I is functional, the electron is circulated within the photosystem and the phosphorylation occurs due to cyclic flow of electrons. A possible location where this could be happening is in the stroma lamellae. While the membrane or lamellae of the grana have both PS I and PS II the stroma lamellae membranes lack PS II as well as NADP reductase enzyme. The excited electron does not pass on to NADP+ but is cycled back to the PS I complex through the electron transport chain. The cyclic flow hence, results

125530.subject: Botany
125530.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Living organisms have the ability to carry energy and store it from oxidisable substances Reason: Water splitting complex is associated with the PS II, which itself is physically located on the outer side of the membrane of the thylakoid
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
125530.sol: Living organisms have the capability of extracting energy from oxidisable substances and store this in the form of bond energy. Special substances like ATP, carry this energy in their chemical bonds.

125609.subject: Botany
125609.text: In the Hatch-Slack pathway, the C₄ acid formed in the mesophyll cells is transported to the bundle sheath cells. What is the immediate primary metabolic event that this C₄ acid undergoes upon entering the bundle sheath cells?
125609.sol: In the C₄ pathway (Hatch-Slack pathway), the C₄ acid (such as malic acid or aspartic acid) formed in the mesophyll cells is transported to the bundle sheath cells. Upon entering the bundle sheath cells, these C₄ acids undergo decarboxylation. They are broken down to release CO₂ and a 3-carbon molecule. The released CO₂ then enters the Calvin cycle ( C₃ pathway) catalyzed by RuBisCO, while the 3-carbon molecule is transported back to the mesophyll to regenerate PEP. Answer: Decarboxylation

125754.subject: Botany
125754.text: Energy transfer in photosynthesis occurs as
options: Chlorophyll b Carotenoid Phycoerythrin Chlorophyll a
Chlorophyll b Carotenoid Phycocyanin Chlorophyll a
125754.sol: Photosynthetic pigments mainly occur on thylakoid membranes. These are major pigments like chlorophylls and accessory pigments like phycoerythrin, phycocyanin, and carotenoids. The accessory pigments absorb light energy of various wavelength and get excited and transfer the energy to chlorophyll-a molecule through electron spin resonance. Order of energy transfer in photosynthesis occur as phycocyanin followed by phycoerythrin followed by carotenoids and finally to chlorophylls.

126051.subject: Botany
126051.text: Identify and name w,x,y and z respectively
options: 2 polar nuclei, Antipodals, Synergids, Egg, Central cell
Synergids, Egg, Central cell, 2 polar nuclei, Antipodals
Egg, Central cell, 2 polar nuclei, Antipodals, Synergids

126137.subject: Botany
126137.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: The zygote gives rise to the proembryo and subsequently to the globular, heart-shaped and mature embryo Reason: A typical dicotyledonous embryo, consists of an embryonal axis and two cotyledons
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
126137.sol: The zygote gives rise to the proembryo and subsequently to the globular, heart-shaped and mature embryo. A typical dicotyledonous embryo, consists of an embryonal axis and two cotyledons

126165.subject: Botany
126165.text: Condition Examples A. Free nuclear endosperm 1. Maize B. Endosperm present 2. Coconut water C. Cellular endosperm 3. White kernel D. Endosperm absent 4. Groundnut
126165.sol: Endosperm is present in rice, wheat, castor and maize Endosperm is absent in pea, bean and groundnut Free nuclear endosperm is present in coconut water and cellular endosperm is present in white kernel part

126239.subject: Botany
126239.text: Match List I with List II regarding pollination mechanisms and floral rewards. List I (Plant) List II (Characteristic/Reward) A. Corn cob I. Pollination at water surface B. Vallisneria II. Obligate symbiotic relationship with a moth C. Amorphophallus III. Feathery stigma to trap airborne pollen grains D. Yucca IV. Provides a safe place to lay eggs Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
126239.sol: A. Corn cob: The tassels seen in corn cobs are the stigma and style which wave in the wind to trap airborne pollen grains, an adaptation for wind pollination. B. Vallisneria: It is a submerged aquatic plant where the female flower reaches the surface of water by a long stalk, and pollination occurs at the water surface. C. Amorphophallus: It is an insect-pollinated plant where the floral reward is providing a safe place to lay eggs within its tall flower. D. Yucca: It has an obligate symbiotic relationship with a s

126735.subject: Botany
126735.text: Starch gives a characteristic blue colour when treated with iodine solution. Which of the following structural features of starch is responsible for this phenomenon?
options: It is a heteropolymer composed of multiple types of monosaccharides.
It forms covalent bonds with iodine molecules upon reaction.
It forms helical secondary structures that can hold iodine molecules.
It consists of highly branched chains without any secondary structure.
126735.sol: According to NCERT, starch forms helical secondary structures. These helices act as a trap, holding the iodine ( I₂ ) molecules inside the helical portion, which results in the characteristic blue colour. Starch does not form covalent bonds with iodine, nor is it a heteropolymer (it is a homopolymer of glucose). While amylopectin in starch is branched, it is the presence of helical secondary structures that allows it to hold iodine. Answer: It forms helical secondary structures that can hold iodine molecules.

126863.subject: Botany
126863.text: Which one of the following pair of nitrogenous bases of nucleic acids, is wrongly matched with the category mentioned against it?
126863.sol: DNA and RNA the principal genetic materials of living organisms are chemically called nucleic acids. These are polymers of nucleotides. Each nucleotide is composed of phosphoric acid, pentose sugar and nitrogenous base. The nitrogenous bases are of two types, ie, purine and pyrimidines. Purines are heterocyclic and two rings compound, eg, adenine, guanine. Pyrimidines are single ring compound, eg, thymine, cytosine, uracil.

127094.subject: Botany
127094.text: The soil which is transported by wind is known as
127094.sol: Soil transportation by wind is common in dry regions where soil is chiefly sandy and the vegetation is very poor. Transported soils are those where the weathered material is taken away at other places. Depending on the nature of these transporting agents the transported soil may be (i) Glacial transportation by glaciers (large mass of snow ice) (ii) Eolian Transportation by wind (iii) Alluvial Transportation by running water (iv) Colluvial Transportation by gravity.

127099.subject: Botany
127099.text: Ozone depletion in stratosphere would result in
127099.sol: In the atmosphere (stratosphere), about 30 km above the surface of the earth, the ozone molecules ( O ₃ ) form an umbrella. It prevents the penetration of harmful ultra violet radiation from the sun and thus protects the life on earth. It is now feared that there is danger of depletion of the ozone layer. The prime suspects of ozone thining or depletion are chlorofluoro carbons (CFCs). Because it is odourless, invisible, that is why it is widely used in domestic refrigerators and cold storage facilities. It is calc

127307.subject: Botany
127307.text: Read the following statements and choose the following option: 1. Biodiversity conservation is no longer a global concern. 2. India has more than 1,000 genetically different strains of rice, and 50,000 varieties of mango. 3. The importance of biodiversity for survival is now being recognized globally. 4. Rauwolfia vomitoria produces resperine
127307.sol: Biodiversity and its conservation are now vital environmental issues of international concern as more and more people around the world begin to realise the critical importance of biodiversity for our survival and well-being on this planet."

127732.subject: Botany
127732.text: Productivity Term Definition A. Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) 1. Biomass available for consumption by heterotrophs B. Net Primary Productivity (NPP) 2. Rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis C. Secondary Productivity 3. Rate of new organic matter formation by consumers D. Decomposition 4. Breakdown of complex organic matter into inorganic substances
127732.sol: Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) (A) is the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis (2). Net Primary Productivity (NPP) (B) is the biomass available for consumption by heterotrophs (1). Secondary Productivity (C) is the rate of new organic matter formation by consumers (3). Decomposition (D) is the breakdown of complex organic matter into inorganic substances (4).

127751.subject: Botany
127751.text: The amount of organic matter or biomass that is generated by producers per unit area over a span of time is called ___
127751.sol: The amount of organic matter or biomass that is generated by producers per unit area over a span of time is called primary productivity.

127902.subject: Zoology
127902.text: What is the ability of frogs to change colour called?
127902.sol: Frogs can live both on land and in freshwater and belong to class Amphibia of phylum Chordata. The most common species of frog found in India is Rana tigrina. They do not have constant body temperature i.e., their body temperature varies with the temperature of the environment. Such animals are called cold blooded or poikilotherms. You might have also noticed changes in the colour of the frogs while they are in grasses and on dry land. They have the ability to change the colour to hide them from their enemies (camo

128200.subject: Zoology
128200.text: Assertion : Gap junctions perform cementing function to keep the neighbouring cells together. Reason : Tight junctions facilitate the cells to communicate with each other by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells, for rapid transfer of ions, small and big molecules, etc.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
128200.sol: Gap junctions are direct cytoplasm to cytoplasm connections between many kinds of animal cells, these are meant for chemical exchange between cells. Whereas tight junctions are the regions where membranes of adjacent animal cells are held close together by sealing strands. They lie cells firmly and check movement of materials between them.

128262.subject: Zoology
128262.text: What are the secretions produced by endocrine glands called?
128262.sol: Endocrine glands lack ducts and are hence, called ductless glands. Their secretions are called hormones. The classical definition of hormone as a chemical produced by endocrine glands and released into the blood and transported to a distantly located target organ has current scientific definition as follows: Hormones are non-nutrient chemicals which act as intercellular messengers and are produced in trace amounts. The new definition covers a number of new molecules in addition to the hormones secreted by the organ

128318.subject: Zoology
options: A condition where the rate of synthesis and secretion of thyroid hormones is increased to abnormal high levels
A form of hyperthyroidism, characterised by enlargement of the thyroid gland, protrusion of the eyeballs, incr
A condition where the thyroid gland secretes a protein hormone called thyrocalcitonin
128318.sol: Exophthalmic goitre is a form of hyperthyroidism, characterised by enlargement of the thyroid gland, protrusion of the eyeballs, increased basal metabolic rate, and weight loss, also called Graves’ disease. It is due to cancer of the thyroid gland or due to development of nodules of the thyroid glands.Thyroid hormones play an important role in the regulation of the basal metabolic rate. These hormones also support the process of red blood cell formation. Thyroid hormones control the metabolism of carbohydrates, pro

128692.subject: Zoology
128692.text: Which vitamin is associated with the maintenance of bone density?
128692.sol: Bone density is the amount of bone mineral present in bone tissue. The higher the bone mineral content, the denser the bones are. Several vitamins are important to bone health. Vitamin B ₁₂ has an effect on bone building cells. The low levels of B ₁₂ result in the higher risk of osteoporosis in both men and women and thus results in lower bone density. Vitamin C is essential for the formation of collagen, the foundation that bone mineralization is built on. Increased levels of vitamin C results in greater bone dens

128942.subject: Zoology
128942.text: What is the effect of Coronary Artery Disease?
options: No effect on lumen of arteries
128942.sol: Coronary Artery Disease, often referred to as atherosclerosis, affects the vessels that supply blood to the heart muscle. It is caused by deposits of calcium, fat, cholesterol and fibrous tissues, which makes the lumen of arteries narrower.

129633.subject: Zoology
129633.text: Kidney Structure Role A. Afferent Arteriole 1. Collects filtrate from glomerulus B. Efferent Arteriole 2. Supplies blood to the glomerulus C. Podocytes 3. Forms filtration slits D. Bowman’s Capsule 4. Drains blood away from the glomerulus
129633.sol: The afferent arteriole supplies blood to the glomerulus. The efferent arteriole drains blood away from the glomerulus. Podocytes form filtration slits in the glomerulus. The Bowman’s Capsule collects the filtrate from the glomerulus.

129816.subject: Zoology
options: The contraction of internal intercostal muscles
The relaxation of external intercostal muscles
129816.sol: Breathing involves two stages : inspiration during which atmospheric air is drawn in and expiration by which the alveolar air is released out.The movement of air into and out of the lungs is carried out by creating a pressure gradient between the lungs and the atmosphere. Inspiration can occur if the pressure within the lungs (intra-pulmonary pressure) is less than the atmospheric pressure, i.e., there is a negative pressure in the lungs with respect to atmospheric pressure. Similarly, expiration takes place when t

130033.subject: Zoology
130033.text: Regarding the functions of our respiratory system, mark the wrong entry.
130033.sol: The respiratory system has no role in cleaning the air.

130135.subject: Zoology
130135.text: The exchange of gases in the alveoli of the lungs takes place by
130135.sol: Oxygen diffuses from alveoli to deoxygenated blood, and carbon dioxide diffuses from deoxygenated blood to alveoli by simple diffusion. Diffusion is defined as, the flow of the substance (gases) from a region of their higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.

130377.subject: Zoology
130377.text: Read the following statements and choose the following option: 1. In resting state the active binding sites on actin is open 2. Thick filament is composed of monomers of proteins. 3. Fascicles are held together by a common collagenous connective tissue layer called fascia. 4. A neural signal reaching Neuromuscular junction releases a neurotransmitter (Acetyl choline) which generates an action potential in the sarcole
130377.sol: Each myosin (thick) filament is also a polymerised protein. Many monomeric proteins called Meromyosins.,A neural signal reaching this junction releases a neurotransmitter (Acetyl choline) which generates an action potential in the sarcolemm,Increase in Ca++ level leads to the binding of calcium with a subunit of troponin

130446.subject: Zoology
130446.text: The first vertebra of the human vertebral column is the ________ and it articulates with the ________.
130446.sol: The first cervical vertebra is the atlas. It articulates with the two occipital condyles of the skull, which is a characteristic feature of the human dicondylic skull. The axis is the second cervical vertebra, not the first. The parietal bones are part of the cranial vault and do not articulate with the vertebral column. The odontoid process is a feature of the axis vertebra itself, not a skull structure that the first vertebra articulates with. Answer: Atlas; occipital condyles

130570.subject: Zoology
130570.text: What is the main purpose of barrier methods in contraception?
options: To prevent ovum and sperms from physically meeting
130570.sol: Condoms are barriers made of thin rubber/ latex sheath that are used to cover the penis in the male or vagina and cervix in the female, just before coitus so that the ejaculated semen would not enter into the female reproductive tract. This can prevent conception. ‘Nirodh’ is a popular brand of condom for the male. Use of condoms has increased in recent years due to its additional benefit of protecting the user from contracting STIs and AIDS. Both the male and the female condoms are disposable, can be self-inserted

130889.subject: Zoology
130889.text: What is essential for maturation and motility of sperms?
options: The secretion of epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicle and prostate
130889.sol: Sperms released from the seminiferous tubules, are transported by the accessory ducts. Secretions of epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicle and prostate are essential for maturation and motility of sperms . The seminal plasma along with the sperms constitute the semen. The functions of male sex accessory ducts and glands are maintained by the testicular hormones (androgens).

131085.subject: Zoology
131085.text: Read the following statements and choose the correct option: 1. The oviducts, uterus and vagina constitute the female accessory ducts 2. Each fallopian tube is about 30-70 cm long and extends from the periphery of each ovary to the uterus 3. The edges of the infundibulum possess finger-like projections called fimbriae, which help in collection of the ovum after ovulation 4. The infundibulum leads to a wider part of t
131085.sol: The oviducts, uterus and vagina constitute the female accessory ducts. Each fallopian tube is about 10-12 cm long and extends from the periphery of each ovary to the uterus. The edges of the infundibulum possess finger-like projections called fimbriae, which help in collection of the ovum after ovulation. The infundibulum leads to a wider part of the oviduct called ampulla

131305.subject: Zoology
options: B-Yolk sac Prevents desiccation of embryo
131305.sol: Placenta is the intimate connection between the fetus and uterine wall of the mother to exchange the materials. The outer surface of the chorion in humans develops a number of finger like projections, known as chorionic villi, which grow into the tissue of the uterus. These villi, penetrate the tissues of the uterine wall in which they are embedded, make up the organ known as the placenta by means of which the developing embryo obtains nutrients and oxygen and gets rid of carbon dioxide and metabolic wastes. Becaus

131933.subject: Zoology
131933.text: Percentage of recombination between A and B is 9 %, ~A and C is 17 %, ~B and C is 26 % , then the arrangement of genes is
131933.sol: 1 map unit or centimorgan is equivalent to 1 % recombination between two genes. The frequency of recombination can be used to depict the arrangement of the genes. Recombination frequency between three genes is A - B =9 %, ~A - C =17 % and B-C=26 % By manipulating the three possibilities of their arrangements it can be concluded that the three genes must be arranged in the order B - A - C with distance between B - A being 9 ~cm , ~A - C being 17 ~cm and B - C being 26 ~cm .

132538.subject: Zoology
132538.text: Assertion : Chimpanzee is the closest relative of the present day humans. Reason : .The banding pattern in some autosomes of man and chimpanzee is remarkably similar.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
132538.sol: It has been observed that the banding pattern of some human chromosomes is very similar to the banding pattern of the corresponding chromosomes in apes. It shows common origin of man and chimpanzee and their close relatedness.

132584.subject: Zoology
132584.text: One of the genes present exclusively on the X chromosome in humans is concerned with
132584.sol: The most common form of red-green colour blindness is an ' X chromosome linked recessive' disorder. The 'red' and 'green' genes are known to reside at the tip of the long arm of the X chromosome. Women have two copies of the X-chromosome, and so they may have normal colour vision, even if they carry one copy of the defective gene. Men have only one X-chromosome, and so will be colour blind.

132689.subject: Zoology
132689.text: What do similarities in proteins and genes among diverse organisms suggest?
options: That organisms are from different evolutionary backgrounds
That organisms share a common ancestry
That organisms have evolved in isolation
That organisms have no evolutionary relationships
132689.sol: Hence, analogous structures are a result of convergent evolution - different structures evolving for the same function and hence having similarity. Other examples of analogy are the eye of the octopus and of mammals or the flippers of Penguins and Dolphins. One can say that it is the similar habitat that has resulted in selection of similar adaptive features in different groups of organisms but toward the same function: Sweet potato (root modification) and potato (stem modification) is another example for analogy.

132957.subject: Zoology
132957.text: Adaptive radiation in placental mammals and Australian Marsupials leading to similarity between distant species is an example of __________.
132957.sol: Adaptive radiation in placental mammals and Australian marsupials occurred independently in isolated geographical areas. When more than one adaptive radiation occurs in an isolated geographical area, leading to the evolution of similar features in distantly related groups to adapt to similar habitats, it is termed convergent evolution. Examples include the placental wolf and the Tasmanian wolf, which show morphological similarities despite being distantly related.

133059.subject: Zoology
133059.text: The concept of chemical evolution is based on
options: interaction of water, air and clay under intense heat
effect of solar radiation on chemicals
possible origin of life by combination of chemicals under suitable environmental conditions
133059.sol: Concept of chemical evolution refers to origin of life from non living matter. First inorganic compounds and then organic compounds were formed in accordance with ever changing environmental conditions.

133344.subject: Zoology
133344.text: The cells called HlV factory are
133344.sol: After getting into the body of the person, the virus enters into macrophages where the RNA genome of the virus replicates to form viral DNA with the help of the enzyme reverse transcriptase. This viral DNA gets incorporated into the host cell’s DNA and directs the infected cells to produce virus particles (Figure 8.6). The macrophages continue to produce viruses and in this way acts like a HIV factory. Simultaneously, HIV enters into helper T-lymphocytes , replicates and produces progeny viruses.

133941.subject: Zoology
133941.text: Which one of the following is not a nitrogen-fixing organism?
133941.sol: Anabaena, Nostoc and Azotobacter are the cyanobacteria. All are nitrogen-fixing organism.

134125.subject: Zoology
134125.text: What is the function of disulphide bridges in insulin?
options: To link two short polypeptide chains together
134125.sol: In mammals, including humans, insulin is synthesized as a pro-hormone (like a pro-enzyme, the pro-hormone also needs to be processed before it becomes a fully mature and functional hormone) which contains an extra stretch called the C peptide. This C peptide is not present in the mature insulin and is removed during maturation into insulin.The main challenge for production of insulin using rDNA techniques was getting insulin assembled into a mature form. In 1983, Eli Lilly an American company prepared two DNA seque

134503.subject: Zoology
134503.text: What is the main reason for DNA being unable to pass through cell membranes?
options: cannot enter the bacterium through pores in its cell wall
134503.sol: Since DNA is a hydrophilic molecule , it cannot pass through cell membranes. Why? In order to force bacteria to take up the plasmid, the bacterial cells must first be made ‘competent’ to take up DNA. 6a252ff098efbb6c17e9298a.subject: Physics
6a252ff098efbb6c17e9298a.text: A car battery has an electromotive force of 12 V and an internal resistance of 0.4 . When it is connected to a headlight of resistance 5.6 , what is the potential difference across the terminals of the battery?
6a252ff098efbb6c17e9298a.sol: Given electromotive force E = 12 V , internal resistance r = 0.4 , and external resistance R = 5.6 . The current in the circuit is given by I = E R + r . Substituting the given values, I = 12 5.6 + 0.4 = 12 6.0 = 2 A . The potential difference across the terminals of the battery is V = IR . Substituting the values, V = 2 5.6 = 11.2 V . Answer: 11.2 V

6a0e277a165ae1327797b3f2.sol: The heart of a frog is a muscular structure situated in the upper part of the body cavity. It has three chambers, two atria and one ventricle. The sinus venosus is a triangular structure attached dorsally to the heart. It receives deoxygenated blood from the major veins called vena cava. The sinus venosus opens directly into the right atrium. The right atrium then pumps this deoxygenated blood into the ventricle. Answer: Right atrium

95483.text: From the following select the characteristic feature that is not correct for Balanoglossus?
options: Belongs to phylum that links non-chordates to chordates.
95483.sol: Balanoglosus belongs to the phylum Hemichordata which connects non-chordates to chordates. This wormlike marine animal has organ system level of organisation. The circulation in it is not closed, rather open type. The coelomic evagination within the proboscis is considered as excretory organ. This animals displays external mode of fertilization. It also shows a collar and a trunk as a body part.

95573.subject: Botany
95573.text: Which of the following animals is not a pair of poikilotherms?
95573.sol: Fishes (like Labeo , Torpedo , Pristis , Carcharodon , Scoliodon , Trygon ), Amphibians ( Rana ) and Reptiles ( Naja ) are poikilotherms but Pteropus (mammal) is a homeotherm.

95670.subject: Botany
95670.text: The main difference in Gram +ve and Gram -ve bacteria resides in their
95670.sol: Bacteria can be classified into two groups on the basis of the differences in the cell envelopes and the manner in which they respond to the staining procedure developed by Christian Gram. Gram staining is a differential staining method that separates bacteria into two categories based on the cell wall composition. Those that take up the Gram stain are called Gram-positive and the other that does not takes up Gram stain are called Gram-negative bacteria.

95705.subject: Botany

95705.sol: The first stable product of the TCA cycle/Kreb's cycle is citric acid which is commercially produced using Aspergillus niger. This fungus belongs to Ascomycetes.

96533.subject: Botany
96533.text: Danny ate spinach, salad and mutton curry for lunch. At which of the following trophic levels did Danny function in this food chain? (i) Producer (ii) Primary Consumer (iii) Secondary Consumer (iv) Tertiary Consumer
96533.sol: Plants are the producers in the food chain. The organism consuming plants is the Primary consumer. The organism consuming animals which in turn derive energy from plants is a Secondary consumer. Thus in the above example Danny is consuming plants is a primary consumer as well as he had mutton which comes from goats which are dependent on plants for their food and acts as the secondary consumer also.

Modification of adventitious root for food storage
Modification of stem for food storage

96827.sol: Rhizome is horizontal underground plant stem capable of producing the shoot and root systems of a new plant. Rhizomes are used to store starches and proteins (ginger, banana, turmeric, etc).

97009.text: The structure which holds the leaf blades and helps to flutter in wind known as a __________
97009.sol: The petiole is a long thin flexible structure that holds leaf blades and flutter in wind. Sometimes petiole becomes tendril and leaf-like. A stipule is a small leaflike appendage to a leaf, typically borne in pairs at the base of the leaf stalk. Lamina is the leaf blade. The swollen leaf base is known as pulvinus.

97354.subject: Botany
97354.text: Biennials get changed into annuals by
97354.sol: Vernalization is a process in which the plants are exposed to certain periods of low temperature so that flowering can be induced in them. Biennials are plants that take two years to complete its life cycle. When these plants are subjected to artificial cold treatment and the correct temperature and photoperiods, they induce flowering in the first growing season itself, just like the annuals (biennials usually flower in the second year of their growing season).

97920.subject: Botany
97920.text: The most widely accepted theory of ascent of sap in trees is
97920.sol: Transpiration pull and cohesion theory was put forward by Dixon and Jolly in 1894. Substitute the given values into the definition: J(8, 12) = ₀^ x^7 (1+x)²⁰ dx J(9, 11) = ₀^ x^8 (1+x)²⁰ dx Adding the two integrals, we get: J(8, 12) + J(9, 11) = ₀^ x^7 + x^8 (1+x)²⁰ dx Factor out x^7 in the numerator: J(8, 12) + J(9, 11) = ₀^ x^7(1+x) (1+x)²⁰ dx Cancel the common factor (1+x) : J(8, 12) + J(9, 11) = ₀^ x^7 (1+x)¹⁹ dx Now, match this result with the definition of J(a,b) : The numerator is x^ a-1 = x^7 a = 8 The denominator is (1+x)^ a+b = (1+x)¹⁹ a+b
